newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to take WTO actions, says Fischer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to take WTO actions, says Fischer.

text.p: Australia will take action in the World Trade Organisation (WTO) against Hungary over agricultural export subsidies, Trade minister Tim Fischer said on Tuesday.
The move was part of steps by Australia to use the WTO's dispute settlement process more actively to challenge unfair barriers to exports, he told a Foreign Correspondent's Association lunch.
Australia would also take action to allow it to put its views opposing U.S. import restrictions on prawns to a panel sought by Malaysia and Thailand, he said.

Fischer, the deputy prime minister, said Australia, New Zealand, Argentina and the U.S. would formally request that a WTO panel on the Hungarian subsidies by set up at a meeting of the WTO dispute settlement body on Wednesday.
"We have already held consultations with Hungary, but regretably it has not been possible to satisfactorily resolve the issue," he said.
On prawns, Fischer said the U.S. prohibited prawn imports from countries not using devices designed to stop turtles being caught accidentally.
"Australia is committed to environmentally responsible fishing methods and supports the U.S. goal of turtle conservation," he said.
"However, we consider that the U.S. approach fails to take into account differing circumstances in prawn harvesting regions."
Although Australia exported only about A$1 million worth of prawns to the U.S., it was concerned the U.S. action could force competitors to sell their prawns into Australia's major markets.
Australia is already involved in a third WTO panel which is examining U.S. and Canadian complaints about European restrictions on meat produced using hormonal growth promotants.

Although Australia has met European Union requirements to export beef, it believed the EU had not based its measures on accepted international standards and that sanitary measures should be based on scientific principles, he said.
